messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired for gpu-pool-west2a — CUDA_OOM_RATE spike: 18 OOMs in 4m. Check dashboard: https://redwood.ops/incidents/7890123456 :rotating_light:

pagerduty: INC-7890 created — primary oncall: jordan (escalation policy: gpu-pools). PagerDuty link: https://pagerduty.com/incidents/INC-7890

jordan (oncall): ack'd. I'm on it. Initial glance at dashboards — memory contended across pool-west2a, KV cache evictions high. @sam can you pull node logs + nvidia-smi?

sam (sre): looking now. nvidia-smi snapshot: GPU gpu-5 at 100% memory, processes show repeated `CUDA_ERROR_OOM`. Pod list (snippet):
```
NAMESPACE     POD                          GPU_MEM
inference     model-infer-abc-5           16384Mi
inference     model-infer-noisy-42       15800Mi
inference     kv-cache-ttl-7              1200Mi
```
Seeing a noisy customer pod `model-infer-noisy-42` with huge context loads. Logs show long sequences (~5k tokens) + large batch sizes.

maya (oncall): looks like a single tenant sending long sequences at high concurrency. Recommend: 1) reroute cust-42 to low-priority pool, 2) enable fallback smaller model variant on pool-west2a, 3) scale pool by +2 nodes if possible. Also consider enabling sequence-length-based auto-shedder for that tenant.

jordan (oncall): applying routing change: `redwoodctl route update --customer cust-42 --pool low-priority --reason "OOM spike"` — executing now.

deploy-bot: routing rule applied to cust-42 -> low-priority (change-id: ch-7890).

support-bot: Created CS ticket #4567 and notified Customer Success (cc: @support). Customer reports 503s for embeddings API around 03:02 UTC.

sam (sre): pushed fallback variant to pool-west2a: `redwoodctl model deploy redwood-base-8b-quant --pool pool-west2a --scope fallback` — rollout started.

deploy-bot: rollout started for redwood-base-8b-quant to pool-west2a (rollout-id: r-7890).

jordan (oncall): evictions dropping — OOMs down to 2 in last 2m after reroute + fallback. Latency normalization observed for most customers. Still seeing periodic OOMs on gpu-5; draining that node. `kubectl cordon gpu-5 && kubectl drain gpu-5 --ignore-daemonsets`

sam (sre): node gpu-5 drained, autoscaler kicked +1 node, pool capacity +1. Monitoring for >10m.

maya (oncall): I'll take the next handoff. @jordan leave any open action items in the incident doc: https://redwood.ops/incidents/7890123456/notes — taking over oncall until 04:30 UTC.

jordan (oncall): handing off to @maya. Notes: noisy tenant cust-42 rerouted, fallback model deployed, node gpu-5 drained, follow-up tasks: scheduled post-incident perf eval for large-context workloads, consider quota for max context length per tenant.

support-bot: CS ticket #4567 updated: Customer experienced 503s for ~4m window, now restored.

maya (oncall): I'll keep watch for 15m then escalate to infra team if OOMs reappear. If sustained, we'll trigger scale + dedicated capacity offer to the customer.

jordan (oncall): :thumbsup: will add timeline + checks to incident notes. Thanks team.

incident-bot: Incident INC-7890 status -> acknowledged -> in_progress.

-- end thread --
